subject: english
question:
Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'No error'.

You have never loved me; / you have either heart / nor honourable feeling!
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The primary issue in the sentence is the incorrect use of "**either**" instead of "**neither**."
 
• In negative sentences, **"neither...nor"** is used to connect two negative alternatives.
 
• The correct phrase should be "**neither heart nor honourable feeling**," ensuring grammatical correctness and clarity.
 
• Thus, the error is located in **Option 2** of the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"You have never loved me; you have **neither heart nor honourable feeling!**"*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "nor honourable feeling!"** – This part of the sentence is correct when paired with "neither".
 
• **Option 3: "You have never loved me;"** – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
 
• **Option 4: "No error"** – This would be the correct option if there were no mistakes in the sentence, but there is an error in Option 2.
